fixed: The smoke first came out as a flat grey slab with a hard edge along the floor. It is redrawn: lower toward its front as it creeps in, and thinning to nothing toward the camera.
The banknote and the coin poked up huge under the Trainer's close-ups, and the gallery's rail crossed behind every close face. Close shots now leave the gallery and the things on the table out.
The label SUBJECT 112 sat on the bulb. It is at the top left now, clear of it.
One shot past the Copycat's shoulder was a crowd of half faces. It is a close shot of the Cheat now.
In the shot where the Cheat takes the coin the camera had slid off centre and cut the end of the back row. It is centred on the Trainer.
When the Copycat walked in, the camera stood back to take in his walk from the edge and everyone was small for that one shot. The camera now holds on the Trainer and he walks into the picture.
The captions 'Uh.', 'Right.' and 'Ha.' flashed for a fraction of a second. A single quick word now stays with what the same person says next.

Biku saw the Copycat's chair slide in with him as he walked to it, and the arrow of SUBJECT 112 stay behind while he moved. The chair now stands where it is from the first frame, the tip of the arrow goes with him, and the label waits until he is in the picture.
notes: The script's card of the rule (Wait ten minutes. / Take the twenty. / Go home.) is left out: a card fills the middle of the picture and would hide the Trainer's smile, which is the point of that line. The rule is spoken.

The script has the Trainer hand the Cheat the coin. The builder cannot pass a thing from hand to hand, so the coin lies on the table from the start and the Cheat takes it while the Copycat looks up, as the Trainer says 'He's ours.'

No door and no wall clock are in the room: with the gallery behind the table there is no clean place for them in a tall picture. The Copycat walks in from the left, the smoke comes in from the left along the floor, and he looks up, not at a clock.
The Cheat does not shrug: there is no shrug for someone sitting. He stays as he is, which is the calm he is paid for.
The twenty is a green note, the one colour in the room besides the cast and the gold. It can be made a pile of gold if the bait should be gold.
Claude cannot hear: the voices, the music and the three sounds are judged by measurement only. 'One one two' and the names need Biku's ears.
